original_value: Due to the limited generation capacity of power stations, many developing countries frequently resort to disconnecting large parts of the power grid from supply, a process termed load shedding. During load shedding, many homes are left without electricity, causing them inconvenience and discomfort. In this paper, we present a number of optimization heuristics that focus on pairwise and groupwise fairness, such that households (i.e. agents) are fairly allocated electricity. We evaluate the heuristics against standard fairness metrics in terms of comfort delivered to homes, as well as the number of times they are disconnected from electricity supply. Thus, we establish new benchmarks for fair load shedding schemes.

result.paraphrase: Because power stations have limited generation capacity, many developing countries often disconnect large portions of the power grid from supply, a practice known as load shedding. In such periods, many households are left without electricity, leading to inconvenience and discomfort. In this paper, we propose several optimization heuristics centered on pairwise and groupwise fairness so that households, i.e. agents, receive electricity fairly. We assess these heuristics using standard fairness metrics based on the comfort provided to homes and the number of times they are cut off from electricity supply. In doing so, we set new benchmarks for fair load shedding schemes.
